message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Package Builds
on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  push:
      branches:
        - master

jobs:
  build-n-publish:
    name: build and publish packages to PyPI and TestPyPI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
          
      - name: setup python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: 3.15.1

      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-

      - name: build package
        run: pipx run build

      - name: publish to test PyPI
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags') != true
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
            password: ${{ secrets.test_pypi_password }}
            repository_url: https://test.pypi.org/legacy/
            
      - name: publish tagged release to PyPI
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags')
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
            password: ${{ secrets.pypi_password }}",
  "rationale": "The workflow repeatedly downloads Python build dependencies (setuptools, setuptools_scm, wheel) via `pipx run build` on every run. Adding a pip dependency cache keyed on `pyproject.toml` reuses those downloads across runs, matching the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) with measured ~9% elapsed savings in a comparable Python workflow. The change is minimal, preserves all build/publish steps and required checks, adds no new network access or privileged actions, and does not weaken permissions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
